Nothing in it is wrong and nothing in it was decided.\n\nThis skill replaces those defaults with decisions, in four ways:\n\n1. **A script deals the directions, you choose among them.** Asked to invent a look, a model picks\n   the category default every time. `scripts/draw.mjs` deals three of twenty researched directions;\n   you choose the one that carries the subject's idea, and the script then deals its type system,\n   palette, hero and section compositions from a library distilled from 247 real sites.\n2. **The idea comes from the subject.** In the study, what separated the best sites from the forgettable\n   ones was a concept taken from the thing itself, not the styling.\n3. **A house style with no ornaments,** measured in a real browser by `scripts/inspect.mjs`, so the\n   rules are checked rather than hoped for.\n4. **You look at what you made.** Screenshots at three widths, a juror's rubric, fix, look again.\n\nOne warning learned in testing. Taking the ornaments away is only half the job; a page that has lost its\nlabels, rules and cards and gained nothing in their place reads as thin, and blind jurors rightly prefer\na richer page with tells over an empty page without them. The other half is substance: type set\nlarger, whole fields of colour, real pictures of this subject's world (found or drawn), and every\nsection carrying its full content. The skill is built to give you that; do not trade it for restraint.\n\nIn the commands below `<skill>` is this skill's folder. Run them from the project's root, so the\nworking files land in `.taste-skill/` there. The scripts need Node 22+ and an installed Chrome, Edge\nor Chromium, and install nothing. `assets.mjs` also needs network access; it uses no API keys.\n\n## The run\n\nDo these in order. Steps 1–5 take a few minutes and decide whether the page is any good.\n\n### 1. Read the brief and the project\n\nFind out what is real: the subject, the audience, the one thing the page must get someone to do, the\nstack, any existing brand (colours, fonts, logo), and above all **what imagery truly exists**: the\nproject's own photographs or product shots, a real interface that can be shown, an image generation\ntool you can call, or nothing. Do not plan around pictures you do not have. Nothing of its own is\nrarely nothing at all: the subject's city, street, materials and history are in open archives and\nmuseums, free to use with a credit (step 6, `scripts/assets.mjs`).\n\nIf the request is vague, decide and state your reading in one line instead of asking. Ask only when a\nmissing fact blocks the work (for example, no product name).\n\nThen **inventory the subject** in your notes: eight to twelve things that belong to this client and to\nno competitor. Look for its name and what the name means; its address, door number, street and\nneighbourhood, and what that place looks like (its tiles, signs, paint colours, typefaces on its shop\nfronts, its light, its weather); the numbers in the brief (seats, rooms, minutes to the sea, the\nprice, the year); the constraint it lives with (only one batch a month, closed in winter, by\nappointment); its materials and colours; its rituals and hours (the oven lit at five, the ferry at\nseven); the printed things of its world (a timetable, a label, a ticket, a sign). This list is where\nthe idea comes from in step 4. In blind tests, the page that won each brief was built from an item on\nsuch a list (the client's name and what it means, the street it stands in, the one constraint that\nmakes it what it is), and the pages that lost had a good composition with a category idea. The list\nis also your picture search: each place, material and printed thing on it is a query for step 6.\n\n### 2. Write the argument\n\nBefore any design, list the page as claims with their proof, one line per section, the way\n`references/copy.md` §1 shows. The claims decide which sections exist and in what order. Delete any\nsection that has no claim. This is how you avoid the stock sequence of hero, logos, three features,\ntestimonial, pricing, call to action.\n\n### 3. Draw the direction\n\n```bash\nnode <skill>/scripts/draw.mjs --sector <sector> --brief \"<one line about the subject>\" \\\n  --sections <roles in the order of your argument> [--tone <tone>] [--have <assets>] [--keep palette,type] \\\n  --options 3\n```\n\nThis deals three directions and prints a short summary of each. Hold each one against your inventory:\nwhich way of composing can carry something only this client has? Choose that one, not the most\nfamiliar, and write one line in your notes on why. In testing, a single random direction that did not\nsuit the subject was the commonest cause of a weak page. Then deal the full sheet:\n\n```bash\nnode <skill>/scripts/draw.mjs <the same arguments, without --options> --direction <chosen id>\n```\n\n- `--sector`: `node <skill>/scripts/draw.mjs --list sectors`. Pick the closest.\n- `--sections`: roles from `--list roles` (features, showcase, how-it-works, testimonial, proof, stats,\n  pricing, faq, cta, footer, intro, about, work, gallery, list, contact). The hero is implied.\n- `--tone` (optional): quiet, bold, warm, technical, playful, luxury, editorial. Only pass it when the\n  brief clearly asks for one.\n- `--have`: assets that really exist, comma-separated: `photography` (the project's own photographs of\n  the place, people or work), `product-photo` (photographs of the specific product, or an image tool\n  that can make them), `product-ui` (real screenshots), `illustration`, `video`. Leave it out if you\n  have none: the draw then avoids compositions that depend on them and the sheet says how to fill\n  picture slots honestly (software shows its own interface built in HTML; a product with no photographs\n  is drawn and set among real pictures of its world, never a fake product shot). Pictures you will\n  find in the open collections are not the project's own; leave them out of `--have`.\n- `--keep palette,type`: when the brand already fixes colours or typefaces. The draw then deals only\n  the composition, and you map the brand's values onto the roles.\n\nThe command prints a **direction sheet**. It is the art direction for this build:\n\n- **Adopt it.** Do not blend it with the layout you would have made anyway. If it feels unfamiliar,\n  good: the familiar layout is the one this skill exists to prevent.\n- Redraw one slot (`--redraw hero | type | palette | photos | section:<role> | direction`) only for a\n  reason you can state: it contradicts a stated brand constraint, or needs an asset that does not\n  exist. Never redraw to get something more comfortable. Record every redraw in your report.\n- When a dealt section cannot hold the real content (it compares three plans and there is one price;\n  it wants five quotations and there are none), do not bend the content to fit. List the others with\n  `--alternatives <role>`, pick the one whose assumptions match the content, and take it with\n  `--redraw section:<role>=<id>`.\n- **Check the palette against the subject.** A dealt palette is a set of proportions (one ground, one\n  ink, one accent, fields) as much as a set of colours. If its colours fight the subject's own material\n  (candy pastels for a peat whisky, neon for a mountain hut), redraw the palette once; if the subject\n  has unmistakable colours of its own (its material, the paint of its street, the landscape outside\n  its windows), keep the dealt proportions and take the colours from the subject instead, and say so\n  in the report.\n- Reprint it any time with `node <skill>/scripts/draw.mjs --show`. In a long session, re-read it before each\n  section you build.\n\n### 4. Find the idea\n\nThe direction is a way of composing. The idea is what makes the page belong to this subject and no\nother. Write this sentence in your notes and do not start building until both blanks are filled from\nthe subject itself:\n\n> On this page, **[something that belongs to the subject]** becomes **[the device the direction calls for]**.\n\nPlaces to look for the first blank:\n\n- **Its output.** What does the thing produce? Put the real output on the page as material. (A camera\n  that prints poems delivered its copy as paper slips.)\n- **Its object or shape.** What does it physically look like, in cross-section, in silhouette?\n  Enlarge it, crop it, make it the frame or the one motif.\n- **Its name.** Can the letters hold a photograph, stack into a wall, split to two corners?\n- **Its place.** Is there one view that makes someone want to be there?\n- **Its ritual.** Is there a sequence the page can perform as it scrolls?\n- **Its artefact.** What printed thing already exists in its world: ticket, menu, label, receipt,\n  invitation, folder, manual?\n- **Its opposite.** Which other category owns the feeling this one lacks?\n\nFill the first blank from your inventory (step 1), not from the category. **The competitor test:** put\nthe nearest real competitor in the sentence (the bakery two streets away, another oak furniture maker,\nanother hut on the same mountain). If the sentence still works, the idea belongs to the category: a\nloaf of bread is every bakery; the seven doors of the street this one is named after are only this one.\n\"Clean and modern\" is not an idea. The sites the study's panel scored lowest were the ones whose idea\nwas recorded as \"none beyond the standard formula\".\n\n**One live thing.** Give the page one thing the visitor can do, or that is different for each visit,\nmade from the idea: pick a wood and see the chair in it; type your name and see it cut in the\nfoundry's letters; set the loan and read the real monthly figure; see whether the hut's stove is lit\nright now and how long until the last ferry; choose a size and see it against the room. In blind tests every winning page had one and the jurors named it first. Rules: it uses the subject's real content, it works on a phone with a thumb, it has a plain\nfallback without script, it never blocks reading, and it is one thing, not a playground. It is\nbuilt in step 6 as part of the page, not added as motion in step 9.\n\n### 5. Write the words\n\nWrite the whole page as a copy deck (plain text) before markup, following `references/copy.md`:\n\n- **Every headline fits in two lines or fewer at every width.** Do the arithmetic in copy.md §2 before\n  committing to a sentence: about 32 characters is safe everywhere at a confident size. The studied\n  gallery heroes have a median of 5 words and 32 characters.\n- One supporting sentence. One primary action, named for what it does, as a real button on the first\n  screen.\n- **The first screen answers the visitor's first question in large type.** For an event: what it is,\n  when and where (the dates belong in the headline or at the second size, never only in small text).\n  For a product: what it is and what it costs or does. For a person: who and what they do. Every\n  section the visitor came for (the line-up, the menu, the rooms, the price) has its own heading and\n  its own place in the navigation.\n- **Write the full content.** Every section the brief asks for delivers its information completely:\n  the whole menu with prices, each room with its own details, every speaker and talk, the price with\n  what it includes, an answer for each real question. Thin sections are the commonest reason a clean\n  page loses to a busier one.\n- Sample details are expected where the brief leaves gaps (dish names, room names and rates, project\n  titles) so the design is seen at full density; list them in the report for the client to confirm.\n  Proof is never invented: no customers, quotes, reviews, press, logos or business statistics.\n\n### 6. Build it, still\n\nBuild the page with motion switched off in your head; a page that needs animation to look finished is\nnot finished. Order of work:\n\n1. **Tokens.** Colour and type roles from the sheet as CSS custom properties. Everything downstream\n   references tokens only. `<skill>/assets/base.css` is a neutral foundation you may start from (reset, token\n   names, fluid type steps, grid, focus and selection styles, the motion helpers); it has no look of\n   its own.\n2. **The hero, exactly as the blueprint describes it,** at desktop and at phone width. Get the big\n   thing big and the small things small before anything else exists.\n3. **Each section from its blueprint,** with this project's content. Keep the geometry, change the\n   subject. Neighbouring sections must not share a layout. **Carry the idea into every section,**\n   pricing, FAQ and footer included: the commonest failure in the study, even among good sites, is a\n   distinctive first screen followed by stock blocks.\n4. **Imagery,** in this order of preference:\n   1. the project's own;\n   2. generated, if you have an image tool;\n   3. **real pictures of the subject's world from the open collections,** whenever an honest one\n      exists. Search them with `node <skill>/scripts/assets.mjs \"<query>\"` (Openverse, Wikimedia\n      Commons, the Art Institute of Chicago and the Met; only licences that allow commercial use, by\n      default). Search the inventory, not the category: its street in old postcards, an old map of the\n      neighbourhood, its material up close, its trade in engravings, a museum object of its kind, a\n      botanical plate, a star chart. Use them large and with intent: one archival photograph as the\n      hero, an engraving enlarged into the page's motif, the real map of the street as the contact\n      section. Look at each before choosing; `--get <ref>` downloads it into `assets/` and records\n      its source and licence, and `--credits` prints the credit line for the footer. A found picture\n      shows the world around the client and is never presented as the client's own product, room,\n      dish, person or team;\n   4. **drawn in code from the subject itself,** for what no honest picture exists of (its objects,\n      its tiles, its windows, its product's interface, made as one consistent flat graphic language in\n      the palette's real colours);\n   5. the photographs dealt on the sheet, only where an honestly generic picture fits (the sea for a\n      sea house), never as a stand-in for the subject;\n   6. type and colour alone.\n\n   **The floor, which the inspector checks:** at least four real pictures on the page, usually six to\n   twelve (photographs, archival images, maps, engravings, footage, raster artwork; for software, its\n   cropped interface fragments count too). SVG drawings do not count toward the floor: draw what no\n   picture exists of, and still carry real pictures. Add one moving picture wherever an honest clip\n   exists: search it with `assets.mjs --video \"<query>\"` and use it as a muted loop with a poster\n   frame. Models skip pictures and footage because finding them is work; the page fails without them.\n\n   `references/imagery.md` covers searching, licences and credits, video, drawing, crops and treatments.\n5. **The live thing** from step 4, built into the section where it proves the claim (often the hero\n   or the booking), with real content, a thumb-sized phone version and a plain fallback.\n6. **Fullness.** Look at each desktop screen as a poster: one dominant thing and the content it\n   carries. A screen that is mostly empty ground is an underbuilt section, not a rest; one deliberate\n   rest per page is the limit, and the inspector fails a page with two or more near-empty screens.\n   Running text is in the full ink at 16px or more; grey is for secondary notes.\n7. **States and semantics.** Real links and buttons, visible focus, alt text, a phone layout that is\n   its own composition.\n\nRead `references/type.md`, `references/colour.md` and `references/layout.md` when you need the detail\nbehind a decision; the laws below are the short form.\n\n### 7. Gate\n\n```bash\nnode <skill>/scripts/lint.mjs <source files or folder>\nnode <skill>/scripts/inspect.mjs <url or path/to/index.html>\n```\n\n`lint.mjs` scans source for banned patterns and stock phrases. `inspect.mjs` opens the page in a real\nbrowser at 1440, 768 and 390 pixels, measures it (headline line counts, type sizes, fonts actually\nloaded, colours, rules, shadows, gradients, contrast, overflow) and saves screenshots to\n`.taste-skill/inspect/`. Fix every `FAIL`. Treat each `WARN` as wrong unless you can defend it to a\ndesigner in one sentence. Re-run until there are no `FAIL`s. Do not argue with the meter and do not\nhide things from it. The inspector serves local files over a throwaway local server; if the page must\nalso open straight from the file system, open `index.html` that way once before you finish.\n\n### 8. Look\n\nPassing the gate means nothing banned was measured. It does not mean the page is good. Open the\nscreenshots the inspector lists (every viewport, with your image viewer or Read tool) and critique them\nwith `references/critique.md`: the fourteen passes, the Awwwards-weighted score, the caps. Write the critique\ndown in its format, fix the top three problems, run the inspector again, look again. Three rounds at\nmost.\n\nJudge only the pictures. If a problem is visible in a screenshot, it is real, whatever the code says.\n\n### 9. Move\n\nNow build the motion layer. It is required, and it is more than one fade: the inspector counts the\nelements that really move while the page loads and is scrolled, and fails a page under eight (it warns\nunder sixteen). The layer has four parts:\n\n1. **The signature move** named on the sheet: one, done well.\n2. **An entrance for the parts of every section:** the heading, then the text, then the picture,\n   staggered by 60–90ms, rising 16–32px with opacity, triggered once as the section enters. Not one\n   fade for the whole block, and never content that stays hidden if the script fails.\n3. **Feedback on every control:** press, hover and focus on buttons, links, cards and the live thing.\n4. **One moving picture:** a found clip as a muted loop, a slow scale or drift on a photograph, or a\n   scroll-linked move on the hero picture.\n\nTransform and opacity only; every move has a `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback that keeps the content\nand drops the travel. A move that changes the colour or the layout of whole screens (colour by\nchapter, a pinned story) is part of the composition, so build it in step 6 and let every look round see\nit. `references/motion.md` has the tokens and tested recipes. Then run the inspector once more and check\nevery screenshot for content that failed to appear.\n\n### 10. Report\n\nTell the user, briefly: the direction dealt (name and seed) and any redraws with reasons; the idea\nsentence and the live thing; the final scores from your last critique round and what still falls short;\nevery found picture and clip with its title, creator, licence and source page (`assets.mjs --credits` prints\nthe list) and where its credit sits on the page; which bundled photographs and which drawings stand in\nfor photography (so they can be replaced); and any sample content that must be swapped before launch.\nDo not claim a check you did not run.\n\n## House rules\n\nThese hold on every build, whatever the direction. `inspect.mjs` measures them.\n\n| Rule | Instead |\n| --- | --- |\n| **Headlines: two lines or fewer, at every width.** Every `h1`–`h6`, and the main line of the first screen whatever its tag. | Cut words. Then widen the measure. Size last. |\n| **Statements are paragraphs.** An intro sentence or a quotation set large is marked up as `<p>` or `<blockquote>`, stays at statement size (36px or less on desktop, 24px on a phone) and runs to about 25 words, three lines. | Larger than that it is a headline and the two-line rule applies. In blind tests jurors read a 42px sentence over four lines as a four-line headline. |\n| **No eyebrows.** No small label above a heading, no pill badge above the headline, no \"New ·\" chip. | Put the information in the heading or the first sentence, or drop it. |\n| **No monospace** outside real code blocks. | The text face. Tabular figures where numbers align. |\n| **No index numbering.** No 01 / 02 / 03, no (001), no \"Step 2\". | Order shown by position, size, or the words. A real `<ol>` if order matters. |\n| **No thin rules.** No hairline dividers, no 1px outlined boxes, no grid lines, crosshairs or crop marks. | Space. A step in background tone. A change of scale. A filled shape. |\n| **No gradients.** Not as backgrounds, not on buttons, not in text. | Flat colour, or a real photograph. A neutral scrim under text on a photo is the one exception. |\n| **No shadows on things at rest.** No glows. | A tone step between surfaces. Shadows only on what truly floats: a menu, a dialog. |\n| **No assistant palette.** No yellow-cream ground with terracotta or rust; no violet or indigo. | The dealt palette. |\n| **No tiny uppercase letter-spaced labels.** | Sentence case at a readable size. |\n| **No icon-topped feature cards, no rows of identical cards.** | The dealt section blueprint. |\n| **No glass.** No backdrop blur panels, no floating pill navigation. | A plain bar: wordmark, a few links, one action. |\n| **No emoji, no gradient blobs, no decorative shapes, no fake dashboards of grey bars.** | A real picture, a real interface fragment, or nothing. |\n| **No styled accent word** in a headline (italic, serif, coloured, underlined). | One face, one colour. The words carry the emphasis. |\n| **Two typefaces at most,** usually one. | The dealt type system. |\n\nThree places keep their own conventions and are left alone by the inspector: real code in\n`<pre>`/`<code>` (monospace is correct there), real tables and form fields (they may have lines), and\na real interface fragment whose root carries the attribute `data-ui` (the product's own borders and\nmenus; see `references/imagery.md` §7).\n\nWhy these, honestly. Some are what the study measured: among the 247 sites, those the panel scored\n7.5 or higher used icon feature cards 1% of the time against 28% for sites under 6.5, pill badges 14%\nagainst 34%, gradients 22% against 52%, shadows 24% against 48%, tiny tracked caps 16% against 57%.\nOthers are the owner's taste and go against current gallery fashion: monospace labels, index numbers\nand hairline grids are actually *more* common on award sites than on weak ones, which is exactly why\ngenerators imitate them and why they now read as costume. They are banned here without exception.\n`references/tells.md` keeps the dated registry.\n\nRemoving ornament leaves space. Never fill it with another ornament. Fill it with scale (make the main\nthing larger), with the full content, with a picture made for this subject, or with a field of flat\ncolour. Leave it empty on purpose once per page at most.\n\n## Laws of the craft\n\nShort form. Numbers are from the study unless marked as house style.\n\n**Type**\n- Two or three sizes do the visible work: one very large, one small, nothing in between. Median\n  headline-to-body ratio on the studied sites is 4.3; the best go far beyond (largest type: median\n  8.4vw on the top sites against 5.0vw on the weak ones).\n- Display type: tracking -0.02 to -0.05em, leading 0.85–1.05. Text: 16–20px, leading 1.45–1.6,\n  45–75 characters per line.\n- Five sizes on a page is the ceiling. One family is normal (a third of the studied sites); two is the\n  limit.\n- Left-aligned by default. Centre at most one moment.\n\n**Space**\n- One grid, one pair of tight margins (16–32px), used everywhere; large things run to the edges. Text\n  blocks share two or three left edges on the whole page.\n- The gap between sections is clearly larger than any gap inside one: 120–220px on desktop.\n- Each section has a different composition from its neighbours; none is a card grid.\n\n**Colour**\n- One ground, one ink, one accent. The accent appears on the action and perhaps one other thing.\n- Running text in the full ink. A page set in soft grey reads unfinished.\n- Surfaces are separated by a small step in tone, never by a line or a shadow.\n- A section may change the whole field colour. Nothing fades into anything.\n\n**Imagery**\n- One dominant image beats six small ones. On the top-scored sites the hero media covers at least half\n  the first screen 68% of the time.\n- Same crop ratios, same treatment, square corners unless the direction says otherwise (73% of the\n  studied sites leave media square).\n- No image is better than a placeholder, an icon, or an abstract shape. A picture drawn for this\n  subject, in its colours and with care, is better than either. A real picture of its world, found\n  and credited, is better still.\n- Every found picture is downloaded into the project, credited on the page and listed in the report.\n  None is presented as the client's own.\n- Nothing ever lies on top of a headline or a statement (the inspector fails it).\n\n**Components**\n- Buttons: flat, one fill colour, either square-cornered or fully round, decided once (top sites: 52%\n  square, 23% pill; the 9–16px \"soft\" radius is the weak-site default). Most strong heroes have no\n  button at all, or one.\n- Navigation: wordmark, three to five plain links, one action. No bar chrome.\n- The footer is a designed close, not a sitemap: on most strong sites the name returns at full width.\n\n## Special cases\n\n**An existing brand or design system.** Pass `--keep palette,type`, map the brand's colours and faces\nonto the roles, and take only composition from the draw. The house rules still apply; if the brand\nitself requires a banned device (its logo sits in a gradient, its accent is violet), keep the brand\nasset, say so in the report, and pass `--allow <rule>` to the inspector for that rule only.\n\n**Redesign or review of an existing page.** Run `lint.mjs` and `inspect.mjs` on it first and report\nwhat they find, then critique the screenshots with `references/critique.md`. For a redesign, draw a\ndirection and proceed from step 2, keeping the page's real content and working behaviour.\n\n**A component or a single section, not a page.** Skip the draw unless there is no direction to follow.\nMatch the surrounding design, apply the house rules and the laws, and still inspect the result.\n\n**No checkout, no form backend.** The primary button goes to the real destination when the brief names\none. Otherwise it opens an email with a written subject and body (`mailto:` with the visitor's choices\nfilled in), or, for a shop, it points at `#checkout` and the report says it must be wired before\nlaunch. Never fake a payment form.\n\n**No Chrome or Node 22.** Run `lint.mjs` (Node 18+), take screenshots with whatever browser tool you\nhave, and critique those. Say in the report that the inspector could not run.\n\n**No network.** If `assets.mjs` reaches no source, draw the pictures and say in the report that the\nopen collections could not be searched.\n\n## Files\n\n| File | Read it when |\n| --- | --- |\n| `references/copy.md` | Writing the argument and the copy deck (steps 2 and 5). The two-line arithmetic. |\n| `references/type.md` | Setting type: scales, tracking, measure, loading fonts, pairing. |\n| `references/colour.md` | Applying the palette: roles, proportions, tone steps, dark pages, contrast. |\n| `references/layout.md` | Grid, margins, rhythm, section variety, navigation, footer, the phone composition. |\n| `references/imagery.md` | Choosing, finding, crediting, cropping and treating pictures; what to do with none. |\n| `references/motion.md` | Step 9. Budget, tokens, recipes, reduced motion. |\n| `references/critique.md` | Step 8. How to look, how to score, what to fix first. |\n| `references/tells.md` | The dated registry of generated-page tells and what each is replaced by. |\n| `references/research.md` | The study: method, numbers, what the best and worst sites do. Cite it, do not guess. |\n| `scripts/draw.mjs` | Deals and reprints the direction; `--photos`, `--site <id>` for more references. |\n| `scripts/assets.mjs` | Step 6: searches open collections for real pictures of the subject's world; `--get` downloads with the credit, `--credits` prints them. |\n| `scripts/lint.mjs` · `scripts/inspect.mjs` | The gate. |\n| `assets/base.css` · `assets/base.js` | An optional neutral foundation to build on. |\n| `library/` | The data the draw reads: directions, heroes, sections, type systems, palettes, photographs, studied sites, motions. Do not read it whole; use the script. |\n",
  "bundled-skills/design-taste-frontend/scripts/assets.mjs": "#!/usr/bin/env node\n// tasteskill / assets: find real, openly licensed pictures of the subject's world, and keep their credits.\n//\n// A page without photographs of its own does not have to draw everything. Archives, museums and open\n// collections hold the subject's city and street, its maps, its materials, its trade's history and the\n// museum objects of its kind, free to use with a credit. This searches them without keys and prints what\n// an agent needs to use a picture honestly: a direct image URL, the page it comes from, its size, its\n// creator, its licence and a one-line credit. Then it downloads the chosen ones into the project and\n// records their credits, so the page works offline and credits every picture.\n//\n//   node assets.mjs \"<query>\"                     search every source, licences safe for commercial use\n//        [--source all|openverse|commons|aic|met|museums]    one or several, comma-separated\n//        [--license safe|pd|all|cc0,pd,by,by-sa,...]        safe = CC0, public domain, CC BY, CC BY-SA\n//        [--orientation landscape|portrait|square]  [--min-width 1000]  [--width 1920]  [--limit 5]\n//        [--no-check]                              skip checking that each image loads (faster)\n//        [--json]                                  machine-readable results\n//   node assets.mjs \"<query>\" --video              search for real footage instead (same options, plus\n//        [--res 720]                               the largest rendition to pick, by its short side\n//        [--max-mb 25]                             clips over this are flagged, and --get refuses them\n//   node assets.mjs --get <ref>[,<ref>...] [--to assets] [--name <file name>] [--width 1920] [--res 720] [--max-mb 25]\n//                                                  download into the project and record the credit\n//   node assets.mjs --credits [--to assets]        print the credits for the footer and the report\n//\n// Image sources: Openverse (api.openverse.org: Flickr, Wikimedia Commons, museums and libraries in one\n// index), Wikimedia Commons, the Art Institute of Chicago (public-domain works over IIIF) and The\n// Metropolitan Museum of Art (Open Access). Video sources: Wikimedia Commons (with its web-sized webm\n// transcodes), the Internet Archive (its curated Prelinger Archives of films, public domain or Creative\n// Commons) and the NASA Image and Video Library. Zero dependencies, no API keys. Node 18+ (built-in fetch).\nimport { readFileSync, writeFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, createWriteStream, unlinkSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport { join, resolve, relative } from 'node:path';\nimport { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';\n\nconst UA = 'taste-skill-assets/2.0 (+https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill)';\nconst SELF = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url).split('\\\\').join('/');\nconst CMD = `node ${/\\s/.test(SELF) ? `\"${SELF}\"` : SELF}`;\nconst SOURCES = {\n  openverse: { media: 'image', name: 'Openverse', note: 'one index over Flickr, Wikimedia Commons, museums and libraries' },\n  commons: { media: 'both', name: 'Wikimedia Commons', note: 'archival photographs, old maps, scans of prints and books, places as they look now', videoNote: 'video files with web-sized webm transcodes: places, crafts, processes, nature' },\n  aic: { media: 'image', name: 'Art Institute of Chicago', note: 'public-domain paintings, prints, photographs and textiles, served large' },\n  met: { media: 'image', name: 'The Metropolitan Museum of Art', note: 'public-domain objects, prints, drawings and photographs (Open Access)' },\n  archive: { media: 'video', name: 'Internet Archive', note: 'the Prelinger Archives: industrial, educational, city and home films from the 1920s to the 1970s, mostly long' },\n  nasa: { media: 'video', name: 'NASA Image and Video Library', note: 'footage of the Earth, space, aircraft, launches and laboratories' },\n};\nconst SOURCE_ALIAS = { museums: ['aic', 'met'], wikimedia: ['commons'], artic: ['aic'], chicago: ['aic'], metmuseum: ['met'], ia: ['archive'], internetarchive: ['archive'] };\nconst VIDEO_TYPES = { 'video/mp4': 'mp4', 'video/webm': 'webm' }; // what every current browser plays; Ogg Theora and QuickTime are left out\nconst LICENCES = ['cc0', 'pd', 'by', 'by-sa', 'by-nc', 'by-nd', 'by-nc-sa', 'by-nc-nd', 'other'];\nconst SAFE = ['cc0', 'pd', 'by', 'by-sa'];\nconst LICENCE_ALIAS = { pdm: 'pd', 'public-domain': 'pd', publicdomain: 'pd', 'cc-by': 'by', 'cc-by-sa': 'by-sa', 'cc-zero': 'cc0' };\nconst WEB_TYPES = { 'image/jpeg': 'jpg', 'image/png': 'png', 'image/webp': 'webp', 'image/gif': 'gif', 'image/avif': 'avif', 'image/svg+xml': 'svg' };\nconst PROVIDERS = { flickr: 'Flickr', wikimedia: 'Wikimedia Commons', met: 'The Metropolitan Museum of Art', nypl: 'New York Public Library', rawpixel: 'rawpixel', stocksnap: 'StockSnap', clevelandmuseum: 'Cleveland Museum of Art', brooklynmuseum: 'Brooklyn Museum', sciencemuseum: 'Science Museum Group', europeana: 'Europeana', geographorguk: 'Geograph Britain and Ireland', inaturalist: 'iNaturalist', wordpress: 'WordPress Photo Directory' };\nconst AIC_FIELDS = ['id', 'title', 'artist_title', 'artist_display', 'date_display', 'image_id', 'thumbnail', 'medium_display', 'artwork_type_title', 'is_public_domain'];\nconst AIC_HEADERS = { 'AIC-User-Agent': UA };\n\nconst USAGE = `Find real, openly licensed pictures of the subject's world, download them, keep their credits.\n\n  ${CMD} \"<query>\" [options]\n      --source all|openverse|commons|aic|met|museums   comma-separated; default all\n      --license safe|pd|all|cc0,pd,by,by-sa,...        default safe: CC0, public domain, CC BY, CC BY-SA\n      --orientation landscape|portrait|square\n      --min-width <px>       smallest acceptable full width, default 1000\n      --width <px>           width of the image URL to use or download, default 1920\n      --limit <n>            results per source, default 5 (at most 20)\n      --no-check             do not check that every image loads (faster, less reliable)\n      --json                 machine-readable results\n  ${CMD} \"<query>\" --video [options]   real footage: Wikimedia Commons, Internet Archive, NASA\n      --source all|commons|archive|nasa\n      --res <p>              largest rendition to pick, by its short side, default 720\n      --max-mb <n>           clips over this are flagged and --get refuses them, default 25\n      --min-width <px>       default 640 for video\n  ${CMD} --get <ref>[,<ref>...] [--to assets] [--name <file name>] [--width 1920] [--res 720] [--max-mb 25]\n  ${CMD} --credits [--to assets]\n\nQueries work best in the subject's own words and a medium: \"ghent postcard\", \"ghent old map\", \"azulejo tiles\",\n\"botanical engraving fig\", \"rotterdam harbour 1920\", \"basalt texture\". The museum sources match one or two\nwords best (\"fig\", \"harbour\"). For footage, name the action or the process: \"coffee roasting\", \"timber\nconstruction\", \"river\", \"city street night\".`;\n\n// ---------- arguments ----------\nconst VALUED = new Set(['source', 'sources', 'license', 'licence', 'orientation', 'min-width', 'width', 'limit', 'get', 'to', 'name', 'type', 'res', 'max-mb']);\nconst FLAGS = new Set(['no-check', 'json', 'credits', 'help', 'video']);\nconst args = {}; const words = [];\nconst argv = process.argv.slice(2);\nfor (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {\n  const a = argv[i];\n  if (a === '-h') { args.help = true; continue; }\n  if (!a.startsWith('--')) { words.push(a); continue; }\n  const eq = a.indexOf('=');\n  const key = a.slice(2, eq === -1 ? undefined : eq);\n  if (VALUED.has(key)) {\n    const v = eq === -1 ? argv[++i] : a.slice(eq + 1);\n    if (v === undefined || v === '' || (eq === -1 && v.startsWith('--'))) fail(`--${key} needs a value.`);\n    args[key] = v;\n  } else if (FLAGS.has(key)) args[key] = true;\n  else fail(`Unknown option --${key}.`);\n}\nfunction fail(message) { console.error(`${message}\\n\\n${USAGE}`); process.exit(2); }\nfunction number(key, def, min, max) {\n  if (args[key] === undefined) return def;\n  const n = Number(args[key]);\n  if (!Number.isFinite(n) || n < min || n > max) fail(`--${key} must be a number from ${min} to ${max}.`);\n  return Math.round(n);\n}\nif (args.type !== undefined && !['image', 'images', 'video', 'videos'].includes(String(args.type).toLowerCase())) fail('--type is image or video.');\nconst VIDEO = Boolean(args.video) || /^videos?$/i.test(String(args.type || ''));\nfunction pickSources(value) {\n  const media = VIDEO ? 'video' : 'image';\n  const usable = Object.keys(SOURCES).filter((k) => SOURCES[k].media === media || SOURCES[k].media === 'both');\n  const out = [];\n  for (const s of String(value).toLowerCase().split(',').map((x) => x.trim()).filter(Boolean)) {\n    const found = s === 'all' ? usable : SOURCE_ALIAS[s] || (SOURCES[s] ? '' : ', museums (aic and met)'}, all.`);\n    const wrong = found.filter((x) => !usable.includes(x));\n    if (wrong.length) fail(`${wrong.join(', ')} has no ${media === 'video' ? 'Video' : 'Image'} sources: ${usable.join(', ')}.`);\n    for (const x of found) if (!out.includes(x)) out.push(x);\n  }\n  return out.length ? out : usable;\n}\nfunction pickLicences(value) {\n  const v = String(value).toLowerCase().trim();\n  if (v === 'safe') return SAFE;\n  if (v === 'pd') return ['cc0', 'pd'];\n  if (v === 'all' || v === 'any') return LICENCES;\n  const out = v.split(',').map((x) => x.trim()).filter(Boolean).map((x) => LICENCE_ALIAS[x] || x);\n  const bad = out.filter((x) => !LICENCES.includes(x));\n  if (bad.length || !out.length) fail(`Unknown licence \"${bad.join(', ') || v}\". 'safe'),\n  orientation: pickOrientation(args.orientation),\n  minWidth: number('min-width', VIDEO ? 640 : 1000, 0, 20000),\n  width: number('width', 1920, 200, 4000),\n  limit: number('limit', 5, 1, 20),\n  video: VIDEO,\n  res: number('res', 720, 144, 2160),\n  maxMb: number('max-mb', 25, 1, 2000),\n  check: !args['no-check'],\n  to: resolve(String(args.to || 'assets')),\n  toArg: args.to ? ` --to ${args.to}` : '',\n};\n\n// ---------- small helpers ----------\nconst sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));\nconst short = (s, n) => { const t = String(s || ''); return t.length > n ? t.slice(0, n - 1).replace(/[\\s,;:.-]+$/, '') + '…' : t; };\nconst noQuery = (u) => (u ? Used to keep the museum sources on the subject.\nfunction queryWords(q) { return String(q).toLowerCase().split(/[^\\p{L}\\p{N}]+/u).filter((w) => w && !['the', 'a', 'an', 'of', 'in', 'on', 'at', 'and', 'or', 'for', 'with', 'from', 'to', 'by'].includes(w)); }\nfunction onSubject(wanted, description) {\n  if (!wanted.length) return true;\n  const loose = (s) => String(s).toLowerCase().normalize('NFKD').replace(/\\p{M}/gu, '').replace(/our\\b/g, 'or'); // harbour = harbor\n  const hay = loose(description);\n  const hits = wanted.filter((w) => { const x = loose(w); return hay.includes(x) || (x.length > 4 && hay.includes(x.replace(/(es|s)$/, ''))); }).length;\n  return hits >= (wanted.length >= 3 ? wanted.length - 1 : wanted.length);\n}\nasync function mapLimit(items, n, fn) {\n  const out = new Array(items.length); let next = 0;\n  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(n, items.length) }, async () => { while (next < items.length) { const k = next++; out[k] = await fn(items[k], k); } }));\n  return out;\n}\nasync function getJson(url, ms = 20000, headers = {}) {\n  for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {\n    let r;\n    try { r = await fetch(url, { headers: { 'User-Agent': UA, Accept: 'application/json', ...headers }, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(ms) }); }\n    catch (e) {\n      const timedOut = e.name === 'TimeoutError' || e.name === 'AbortError';\n      if (!timedOut && attempt < 2) { await sleep(800); continue; }\n      throw new Error(timedOut ? `no answer within ${Math.round(ms / 1000)} s` : `could not connect (${e.cause?.code || e.message})`);\n    }\n    if ([502, 503, 504].includes(r.status) && attempt < 2) { await sleep(1200); continue; }\n    if (r.status === 429) throw new Error('rate limited (HTTP 429): wait a minute, or search another --source');\n    if (r.status === 410) throw new Error('this API endpoint has been retired (HTTP 410); assets.mjs needs updating for it');\n    if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${r.status}${r.status >= 500 ? ', the service is having trouble' : ''}`);\n    try { return await r.json(); } catch { throw new Error('the answer was not JSON'); }\n  }\n}\n// Width and height from the first bytes of a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP file.\nfunction dims(b) {\n  if (!b || b.length < 26) return {};\n  if (b[0] === 0x89 && b.toString('ascii', 1, 4) === 'PNG') return { w: b.readUInt32BE(16), h: b.readUInt32BE(20) };\n  if (b.toString('ascii', 0, 3) === 'GIF') return { w: b.readUInt16LE(6), h: b.readUInt16LE(8) };\n  if (b.toString('ascii', 0, 4) === 'RIFF' && b.toString('ascii', 8, 12) === 'WEBP' && b.length >= 30) {\n    const f = b.toString('ascii', 12, 16);\n    if (f === 'VP8X') return { w: 1 + b.readUIntLE(24, 3), h: 1 + b.readUIntLE(27, 3) };\n    if (f === 'VP8L') { const bits = b.readUInt32LE(21); continue; }\n      const m = b[i + 1];\n      if (m === 0xff) { i++; continue; }\n      if (m === 0x01 || (m >= 0xd0 && m <= 0xd8)) { i += 2; continue; }\n      if (m >= 0xc0 && m <= 0xcf && m !== 0xc4 && m !== 0xc8 && m !== 0xcc) return { w: b.readUInt16BE(i + 7), h: b.readUInt16BE(i + 5) };\n      i += 2 + b.readUInt16BE(i + 2);\n    }\n  }\n  return {};\n}\n// Width, height and duration from the head of an MP4 whose index comes first (what web renditions use).\nfunction mp4Info(b) {\n  const out = {}; const h = b.readUInt32BE(end - 4) >>> 16; if (w * h > area) { area = w * h; out.w = w; out.h = h; } }\n  }\n  const m = b.indexOf('mvhd');\n  if (m > 3 && m + 36 <= b.length) {\n    const v1 = b[m + 4] === 1; Reads only the first\n// 128 KB of an image, or 512 KB of a video (enough for an MP4's size and duration).\nasync function probe(url, ms = 15000, video = false, again = true) {\n  const ac = new AbortController(); const timer = setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), ms);\n  const want = video ? 524288 : 131072;\n  try {\n    const headers = video ? { 'User-Agent': UA, Accept: 'video/*' } : imageHeaders(url);\n    const r = await fetch(url, { headers: { ...headers, Range: `bytes=0-${want - 1}` }, signal: ac.signal, redirect: 'follow' });\n    if (!r.ok) {\n      r.body?.cancel().catch(() => {});\n      if (r.status >= 500 && again) { clearTimeout(timer); await sleep(1000); return probe(url, ms, video, false); } // file servers stumble now and then\n      return { ok: false, why: `HTTP ${r.status}` };\n    }\n    const type = (r.headers.get('content-type') || '').split(';')[0].trim().toLowerCase();\n    if (!(video ? ok : pool.filter((h) => !exclude.includes(h.id)).length ? pool.filter((h) => !exclude.includes(h.id)) : pool, recent('hero', 3)));\n}\nfunction dealType(dir, exclude) {\n  let pool = L.type.filter((t) => (dir.type || []).includes(t.id) || (dir.typeClasses || []).includes(t.class));\n  if (!pool.length) pool = L.type;\n  const p = pool.filter((t) => !exclude.includes(t.id));\n  return pick(fresh(p.length ? 3 : 0;\n    if ((set.primary || []).includes(input.sector)) score += 5;\n    // rooms and tables would be taken for this very house: for places to stay, deal the surroundings instead\n    if (mode === 'atmosphere' && ['hospitality', 'real-estate'].includes(input.sector) && id === 'interior-and-table') score -= 6;\n    score += words.filter((w) => (set.keywords || []).some((k) => k === w || (k.length >= 5 && w.startsWith(k)) || (w.length >= 5 && k.startsWith(w)))).length * 4;\n    score += set.photos.filter((ph) => words.some((w) => ph.alt.toLowerCase().includes(w))).length;\n    if (dir.photoTone) score += set.photos.filter((ph) => ph.tone === dir.photoTone).length / set.photos.length;\n    return { id, set, score };\n  }).filter((x) => x.score > 0 && x.set.photos.length >= 5 && (mode !== 'interface' || SOFT_SETS.includes(x.id))).sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score);\n  if (!scored.length) return null;\n  // one set, so the photographs share a subject and a light; choose among the best-fitting few\n  const top = scored.filter((x) => x.score >= scored[0].score * 0.6).slice(0, 4);\n  const chosen = pick(top);\n  let pool = chosen.set.photos;\n  if (dir.photoTone) { const toned = pool.filter((ph) => ph.tone === dir.photoTone || ph.tone === 'mid'); if (toned.length >= 6) pool = toned; }\n  // Without product photographs, a picture of the same kind of thing would pass for the product: deal\n  // those last and mark them. A start only: the better queries come from the builder's inventory.\nfunction assetQueries(input) {\n  const brief = String(input.brief || '');\n  const notPlace = /^(?:january|february|march|april|may|june|july|august|september|october|november|december|monday|tuesday|wednesday|thursday|friday|saturday|sunday)s?$/i;\n  const placeRe = /(?:^|[\\s,(])(?:in|at|near|from|on|above|below|beside|outside|off|over)\\s+(\\p{Lu}[\\p{L}'’-]*(?:\\s+(?:\\p{Lu}[\\p{L}'’-]*|de|da|do|dos|das|di|del|van|von|der|den))*)/gu;\n  const place = [...brief.matchAll(placeRe)].map((m) => m[1].trim()).find((p) => !notPlace.test(p.split(/\\s+/)[0]));\n  const stop = briefStop();\n  const generic = new Set(['seat', 'seats', 'room', 'rooms', 'minute', 'minutes', 'hour', 'hours', 'night', 'nights', 'year', 'years', 'people', 'family', 'local', 'short', 'best', 'making', 'selling', 'serving', 'offering', 'business', 'company', 'brand', 'shop', 'store', 'studio', 'service', 'services', 'dinner', 'lunch', 'breakfast', 'included', 'online', 'modern']);\n  // the subject: the last plain words of the first noun phrase (\"a 38-seat Italian restaurant in ...\" gives \"restaurant\")\n  const words = brief.split(/\\s+/).filter(Boolean); const phrase = [];\n  for (let k = words.findIndex((w) => /^an?$/i.test(w)) + 1; k < words.length; k++) {\n    if (/^(?:in|at|on|for|from|with|near|above|below|by|that|which|who|of|and|to)$/i.test(words[k])) break;\n    phrase.push(words[k].replace(/[,.;:()!?]+$/, ''));\n    if (/[,.;:()!?]$/.test(words[k])) break;\n  }\n  const plain = phrase.filter((w) => /^\\p{Ll}{3,}$/u.test(w) && !stop.has(w) && !generic.has(w));\n  const subject = plain.slice(-2).join(' ') || (input.sector !== 'other' ? out : shuffle(L.sites.filter((s) => s.score >= 7.6)).slice(0, 2);\n}\n\n// ---------- rendering ----------\nfunction siteCard(s, full) {\n  const lines = [`- **${s.name}** (${s.source}, studied score ${s.score}) \\`${s.id}\\``, `  Idea: ${s.idea}`, `  Hero: ${s.hero}`];\n  if (full) {\n    lines.push(`  Type: ${s.type}`, `  Colour: ${s.colour}`, `  Imagery: ${s.imagery}`, `  Layout: ${s.layout}`);\n    for (const sec of s.sections || []) lines.push(`  Section (${sec.role}): ${sec.description}`);\n    for (const t of s.steal || []) lines.push(`  Worth taking: ${t}`);\n    lines.push(`  URL: ${s.url}`);\n  } else if (s.steal?.[0]) lines.push(`  Worth taking: ${s.steal[0]}`);\n  return lines.join('\\n');\n}\nfunction render(s) {\n  const d = s.direction; const o = [];\n  const p = (x = '') => o.push(x);\n  p(`# DIRECTION SHEET — ${d.name}`);\n  p(`seed ${s.seed} · drawn ${s.at.slice(0, 10)}${s.redraws ? Imagery');\n  // where to look for real pictures of the subject's world, with first queries built from the brief\n  const qs = assetQueries(s.input);\n  const find = qs.length\n    ? `\\`${ASSETS_CMD} \"${qs[0]}\"\\`${qs.length > 1 ? `, then ${qs.slice(1).map((q) => `\"${q}\"`).join(' and ')}` : ''}, then queries from your inventory (its street, its materials, its trade's tools and history)`\n    : `\\`${ASSETS_CMD} \"<a place, material or object from your inventory>\"\\``;\n  const MODE = {\n    interface: '**This subject is software and there are no screenshots, so its pictures are its own interface.** Wherever this sheet says photograph, image or object, build a believable fragment of the product in HTML at real size (real labels, numbers that add up, one item hovered or selected), put the attribute `data-ui` on its root, and crop or scale it the way the blueprint treats a photograph: a full-bleed close crop, a tile, the fixed half of a split. If the product works on something physical (ships, plants, buildings, a city), one real picture of that world can carry a section: find it with `' + ASSETS_CMD + ' \"<that world>\"`, download it with `--get`, credit it on the page, and never let it pass for the product or its customers.',\n    'no-product-photo': '**There are no photographs of the product and none can be faked.** Wherever this sheet calls for a picture of the object, draw the object: its pieces as flat shapes in inline SVG, large, in one graphic language and in the colours that make it worth buying (a glaze, a finish, a material), never grey placeholders (references/imagery.md §8). **Around the object, use real pictures of its world** from the open collections: its material up close, its town in old postcards, its craft in engravings, a museum piece of the same kind, never one a visitor could take for the product itself (references/imagery.md §3). In your report, say that product photography is needed and which drawings it will replace, and list every found picture with its source and licence.',\n    atmosphere: '**The project has no photographs of its own yet.** First choice: **real pictures of the subject\\'s world from the open collections**: its city and street in old postcards and photographs, an old map of the neighbourhood, its materials up close, its trade in engravings, museum objects of its kind (references/imagery.md §3). Start with ' + find + '. Download what you use into the project with `--get` and credit every one on the page (`--credits` prints the footer line). One treatment for all of them. 'landscape' : ph.ratio <= 0.87 ? Measurements are clean — now judge the pictures.');\nfor (const [title, list] of [['FAIL — fix every one of these', fails], ['WARN — fix, or be able to defend', warns]]) {\n  if (!list.length) continue;\n  line(title);\n  for (const f of list) {\n    line(`  [${f.id}] @${f.width}px${f.alsoAt ? ' (+' + f.alsoAt.join(', ') + ')' : ''}  ${f.message}`);\n    line(`      → ${f.fix}`);\n  }\n  line('');\n}\nline('LOOK AT THE RENDER — open these with your image viewer / Read tool before saying anything about quality:');\nconst rel = (p) => relative(process.cwd(), p).split('\\\\').join('/');\nfor (const im of report.images) { line(`  ${(im.viewport + ' ' + im.width + 'px').padEnd(15)} ${rel(im.fold)}`); for (const p of im.pages) line(`  ${''.padEnd(15)} ${rel(p)}`); }\nline('');\nline(`report: ${rel(join(outDir, 'report.json'))}`);\nline(fails.length ? `RESULT: ${fails.length} FAIL, ${warns.length} WARN — not done.` : `RESULT: 0 FAIL, ${warns.length} WARN — measurements pass. Passing the meter is the floor, not the grade: score the screenshots with references/critique.md.`);\nprocess.exit(fails.length ? 1 : 0);\n",
  "bundled-skills/design-taste-frontend/scripts/lint.mjs": "#!/usr/bin/env node\n// tasteskill / lint — static scan of source files for the tells this skill bans.\n// Catches them before a render, plus the ones a render cannot see (copy habits, motion values).\n//\n//   node lint.mjs [files or directories ...] [--json]\n//\n// Exit code 1 when any FAIL is found. Zero dependencies.\nimport { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport { join, extname, relative, resolve } from 'node:path';\n\nconst args = process.argv.slice(2);\nconst asJson = args.includes('--json');\nconst roots = args.filter((a) => !a.startsWith('--'));\nif (!roots.length) roots.push('.');\nconst EXT = new Set(['.html', '.htm', '.css', '.scss', '.less', '.js', '.jsx', '.ts', '.tsx', '.vue', '.svelte', '.astro', '.mdx']);\nconst SKIP = new Set(['node_modules', '.git', '.next', '.nuxt', '.svelte-kit', 'dist', 'build', 'out', '.vercel', '.taste-skill', 'coverage', '.turbo', 'vendor']);\n\nconst files = []; const tooBig = [];\nconst walk = (p) => {\n  let st; try { st = statSync(p); } catch { return; }\n  if (st.isDirectory()) { for (const f of readdirSync(p)) if (!SKIP.has(f) && !f.startsWith('.')) walk(join(p, f)); }\n  else if (EXT.has(extname(p)) && !/\\.min\\.|lock|\\.d\\.ts$/.test(p)) { if (st.size < 4000000) files.push(p); else tooBig.push(p); }\n};\nfor (const r of roots) {\n  try { statSync(resolve(r)); } catch { console.error(`Not found: ${r}`); process.exit(2); }\n  walk(resolve(r));\n}\nif (!files.length) { console.error(`No source files (${[...EXT].join(' ')}) under: ${roots.join(', ')}`); process.exit(2); }\nif (tooBig.length) console.error(`Skipped (over 4 MB, check by hand): ${tooBig.join(', ')}`);\n\n// Each rule: [level, id, regex, message]. Tested per line. `code` lines (inside <pre>/<code>) skip the mono rule.\nconst R = [\n  ['FAIL', 'mono', /\\bfont-mono\\b|font-family\\s*:[^;{}]*(mono\\b|monospace|Courier|Consolas|Menlo|Monaco)|(JetBrains|Geist|IBM\\+?Plex|Space|DM|Roboto|Fragment|Azeret|Red\\+?Hat|Martian|Commit|Departure|Fira)[+_ ]?Mono|Geist_Mono|GeistMono|Fira[+ ]Code|ui-monospace/i, 'Monospace type. Only literal code may be monospace.'],\n  ['FAIL', 'gradient', /(linear|radial|conic)-gradient\\(|\\bbg-(gradient|linear|radial|conic)-|\\b(from|via)-(?!\\[?0)[a-z]+-\\d{2,3}\\b/, 'Gradient fill. Use a flat colour or a real image (a neutral scrim over a photo is the one exception).'],\n  ['FAIL', 'gradient-text', /bg-clip-text|background-clip\\s*:\\s*text|text-transparent/, 'Gradient / clipped text. Elements at rest carry none; only real overlays (menu, dialog, sticky bar) may.'],\n  ['FAIL', 'numbering', />\\s*[(\\[]?0[1-9][)\\]]?\\.?\\s*<|[\"'`]\\s*0[1-9]\\s*[\"'`]|decimal-leading-zero|>\\s*(Step|Phase|No\\.?|Chapter)\\s*0?\\d\\s*</i, 'Decorative index numbering (01 / 02 / 03).'],\n  ['WARN', 'numbering', /padStart\\(\\s*2\\s*,\\s*[\"']0[\"']\\s*\\)/, 'Zero-padding in script. Separate with space, tone or scale; lines belong to real tables and form fields.'],\n  ['WARN', 'outlined-box', /border\\s*:\\s*1px\\s+solid|\\bborder\\b(?=[^\"'`]*\\brounded)/, 'A 1px outlined box. Prefer a filled surface or no box.'],\n  ['WARN', 'glass', /backdrop-blur|backdrop-filter\\s*:/, 'Backdrop blur. One sticky bar at most; glass cards are a tell.'],\n  ['WARN', 'copy', /\\b(unlock|unleash|supercharge|seamless(ly)?|elevate|empower(s|ing)?|revolutioni[sz]e|game[- ]chang(er|ing)|cutting[- ]edge|next[- ]gen(eration)?|world[- ]class|best[- ]in[- ]class|all[- ]in[- ]one|effortless(ly)?|blazing(ly)?[- ]fast|lightning[- ]fast|reimagin(e|ed|ing)|delve|tapestry|leverage|synergy|streamline|robust|holistic|turbocharge|transform the way|take your .{1,30} to the next level|say goodbye to|in today'?s|the future of|built for the modern|not just .{1,40}[,—-] (it'?s|but)|more than (just )?a)\\b/i, 'Stock marketing phrase. Say the specific thing the product does.'],\n  ['WARN', 'cta-copy', />\\s*(Learn more|Get started|Click here|Read more|Discover more|Explore now|Submit)\\s*</i, 'Generic button label. Name the action or the thing (\"Book a table\", \"See the plans\").'],\n  ['WARN', 'default-font', /family=(Inter|Poppins|Montserrat|Roboto|Open\\+Sans|Space\\+Grotesk|Instrument\\+Serif|Playfair\\+Display|Plus\\+Jakarta\\+Sans|Outfit|Sora|Lato|Nunito|Raleway)\\b|font-family\\s*:\\s*[\"']?(Inter|Poppins|Montserrat|Roboto|Space Grotesk|Instrument Serif|Playfair Display|Plus Jakarta Sans|Outfit|Sora)\\b|from [\"']next\\/font\\/google[\"'].*\\b(Inter|Poppins|Montserrat|Space_Grotesk|Instrument_Serif|Playfair_Display|Plus_Jakarta_Sans|Outfit|Sora)\\b|\\b(Inter|Poppins|Space_Grotesk|Instrument_Serif|Playfair_Display)\\s*\\(\\s*\\{/, 'A default typeface. Use the faces named by the drawn direction.'],\n  ['WARN', 'transition-all', /transition\\s*:\\s*all\\b|\\btransition-all\\b/, 'transition: all. Name the properties (transform, opacity).'],\n  ['WARN', 'ease-in', /(?<![-\\w])ease-in(?!-out)\\b/, 'ease-in on UI feels sluggish. Use a strong ease-out for enters and exits.'],\n  ['WARN', 'scale-zero', /scale\\(\\s*0\\s*\\)|\\bscale-0\\b/, 'Entering from scale(0). Start at 0.95–0.98 with opacity 0.'],\n  ['WARN', 'h-screen', /\\bh-screen\\b|height\\s*:\\s*100vh/, '100vh jumps on mobile. Use 100svh / 100dvh.'],\n  ['WARN', 'bounce', /animate-(bounce|ping|pulse)\\b/, 'Looping attention animation (bounce / ping / pulse dot).'],\n];\n\nconst findings = [];\nlet emDashes = 0;\nfor (const file of files) {\n  const rel = relative(process.cwd(), file).split('\\\\').join('/');\n  const lines = readFileSync(file, 'utf8').split(/\\r?\\n/);\n  let inCode = false; let selector = ''; let pending = '';\n  lines.forEach((line, i) => {\n    // track the CSS selector we are inside, so rules scoped to [data-ui] (interface fragments) keep their own lines\n    if (line.includes('{')) { selector = pending + line.slice(0, line.indexOf('{')); pending = ''; } else if (!line.includes('}')) pending = (pending + ' ' + line).slice(-300);\n    const inUi = /data-ui/.test(selector) || /data-ui/.test(line);\n    if (line.includes('}') && !line.includes('{')) { selector = ''; pending = ''; }\n    if (/<(pre|code)\\b/i.test(line)) inCode = true;\n    const codeLine = inCode || /<(pre|code|kbd|samp)\\b/i.test(line);\n    if (/<\\/(pre|code)>/i.test(line)) inCode = false;\n    if (line.length > 2000) return; // minified or data\n    if (/taste-skill-ignore/.test(line)) return;\n    if (!/^\\s*(\\/\\/|\\/\\*|\\*|<!--)/.test(line)) emDashes += (line.replace(/\\/\\/.*$|\\/\\*.*?\\*\\/|<!--.*?-->/g, '').match(/—/g) || []).length; // comments are not copy\n    for (const [level, id, re, message] of R) {\n      if (id === 'mono' && (codeLine || /(^|[\\s,>+~(])(pre|code|kbd|samp)\\b|code/i.test(selector))) continue; // real code may be monospace\n      if ((id === 'hairline' || id === 'outlined-box') && /(^|[\\s,>+~(])(table|thead|tbody|tfoot|tr|td|th|input|textarea|select|fieldset)\\b/i.test(selector)) continue; // real tables and form fields keep their lines\n      if (inUi && (id === 'hairline' || id === 'outlined-box' || id === 'shadow')) continue;\n      if (id === 'hairline' && /sr-only|visually-hidden|clip(-path)?\\s*:|outline/i.test(line + selector)) continue; // screen-reader helpers and focus outlines are not rules\n      if ((id === 'copy' || id === 'cta-copy' || id === 'emoji') && /^\\s*(\\/\\/|\\/\\*|\\*|import |@import|<!--)/.test(line)) continue;\n      const m = line.match(re);\n      if (m) findings.push({ level, id, file: rel, line: i + 1, match: m[0].trim().slice(0, 70), message });\n    }\n  });\n}\nif (emDashes > 4) findings.push({ level: 'WARN', id: 'em-dash', file: '(all files)', line: 0, match: `${emDashes} em dashes`, message: 'Em-dash habit. Use a full stop or a comma; keep at most one or two on a page.' });\n\nif (asJson) { console.log(JSON.stringify({ files: files.length, findings }, null, 1)); process.exit(findings.some((f) => f.level === 'FAIL') ? 1 : 0); }\n\nconst byId = new Map();\nfor (const f of findings) { const k = f.level + ' ' + f.id; if (!byId.has(k)) byId.set(k, []); byId.get(k).push(f); }\nconsole.log(`TASTESKILL · LINT   ${files.length} file(s)`);\nif (!findings.length) console.log('\\nNo banned patterns in source. Now run inspect.mjs on the rendered page.');\nfor (const lvl of ['FAIL', 'WARN']) {\n  const keys = [...byId.keys()].filter((k) => k.startsWith(lvl));\n  if (!keys.length) continue;\n  console.log(`\\n${lvl}`);\n  for (const k of keys) {\n    const list = byId.get(k);\n    console.log(`  [${list[0].id}] ${list[0].message}  (${list.length}×)`);\n    for (const f of list.slice(0, 6)) console.log(`      ${f.file}:${f.line}  ${f.match}`);\n    if (list.length > 6) console.log(`      … ${list.length - 6} more`);\n  }\n}\nconst fails = findings.filter((f) => f.level === 'FAIL').length;\nconsole.log(`\\nRESULT: ${fails} FAIL, ${findings.length - fails} WARN${fails ? ' — fix the FAILs before rendering.' : ''}`);\nconsole.log('Interface fragments marked data-ui keep their own borders and shadows. Any other line that must keep a flagged pattern for a real reason can carry the comment taste-skill-ignore.');\nprocess.exit(fails ? 1 : 0);\n",
  "bundled-skills/design-taste-frontend/scripts/lib/cdp.mjs": "// Zero-dependency Chrome DevTools Protocol client.\n// Drives an installed Chrome / Edge / Chromium in headless mode over Node's built-in WebSocket.\n// Requires Node 22+. No npm install.\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { existsSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport { tmpdir } from 'node:os';\nimport { join } from 'node:path';\n\nconst sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));\n\nexport function findChrome() {\n  const env = process.env.CHROME_PATH || process.env.PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH;\n  if (env && existsSync(env)) return env;\n  const home = process.env.HOME || process.env.USERPROFILE || '';\n  const local = process.env.LOCALAPPDATA || '';\n  const pf = process.env.PROGRAMFILES || 'C:\\\\Program Files';\n  const pf86 = process.env['PROGRAMFILES(X86)'] || 'C:\\\\Program Files (x86)';\n  const candidates = [\n    // Windows\n    join(pf, 'Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe'),\n    join(pf86, 'Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe'),\n    join(local, 'Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe'),\n    join(pf86, 'Microsoft/Edge/Application/msedge.exe'),\n    join(pf, 'Microsoft/Edge/Application/msedge.exe'),\n    join(pf, 'BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser/Application/brave.exe'),\n    // macOS\n    '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome',\n    '/Applications/Chromium.app/Contents/MacOS/Chromium',\n    '/Applications/Microsoft Edge.app/Contents/MacOS/Microsoft Edge',\n    '/Applications/Brave Browser.app/Contents/MacOS/Brave Browser',\n    join(home, 'Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome'),\n    // Linux\n    '/usr/bin/google-chrome', '/usr/bin/google-chrome-stable', '/usr/bin/chromium',\n    '/usr/bin/chromium-browser', '/snap/bin/chromium', '/usr/bin/microsoft-edge',\n  ];\n  for (const c of candidates) if (c && existsSync(c)) return c;\n  return null;\n}\n\nexport class Browser {\n  static async launch({ width = 1440, height = 900, extraArgs = [] } = {}) {\n    if (typeof WebSocket === 'undefined') {\n      throw new Error('Node 22+ is required (built-in WebSocket missing). Current: ' + process.version);\n    }\n    const exe = findChrome();\n    if (!exe) {\n      throw new Error('No Chrome/Edge/Chromium found. Install one or set CHROME_PATH to its executable.');\n    }\n    const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'ad-chrome-'));\n    const args = [\n      '--headless=new', '--remote-debugging-port=0', `--user-data-dir=${dir}`,\n      '--no-first-run', '--no-default-browser-check', '--mute-audio', '--hide-scrollbars',\n      '--disable-background-timer-throttling', '--disable-renderer-backgrounding',\n      '--disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows', '--disable-features=Translate,MediaRouter',\n      '--force-color-profile=srgb', '--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required',\n      '--enable-unsafe-swiftshader', `--window-size=${width},${height}`, ...extraArgs, 'about:blank',\n    ];\n    const proc = spawn(exe, args, { stdio: ['ignore', 'ignore', 'pipe'] });\n    const wsUrl = await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n      let buf = '';\n      const t = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('Chrome did not start within 20s')), 20000);\n      proc.stderr.on('data', (d) => {\n        buf += d.toString();\n        const m = buf.match(/DevTools listening on (ws:\\/\\/[^\\s]+)/);\n        if (m) { clearTimeout(t); resolve(m[1]); }\n      });\n      proc.on('exit', (code) => { clearTimeout(t); reject(new Error('Chrome exited early, code ' + code + '\\n' + buf.slice(-600))); });\n    });\n    const b = new Browser();\n    b.proc = proc; b.dir = dir; b.nextId = 1; b.pending = new Map(); b.listeners = new Map();\n    b.ws = new WebSocket(wsUrl);\n    await new Promise((res, rej) => { b.ws.onopen = res; b.ws.onerror = () => rej(new Error('CDP socket failed')); });\n    b.ws.onmessage = (ev) => {\n      const msg = JSON.parse(typeof ev.data === 'string' ? ev.data : Buffer.from(ev.data).toString());\n      if (msg.id && b.pending.has(msg.id)) {\n        const { resolve, reject, timer } = b.pending.get(msg.id);\n        clearTimeout(timer); b.pending.delete(msg.id);\n        if (msg.error) reject(new Error(msg.error.message)); else resolve(msg.result);\n      } else if (msg.method) {\n        const fns = b.listeners.get((msg.sessionId || '') + '|' + msg.method);\n        if (fns) for (const fn of [...fns]) fn(msg.params);\n      }\n    };\n    return b;\n  }\n\n  send(method, params = {}, sessionId, timeoutMs = 30000) {\n    const id = this.nextId++;\n    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n      const timer = setTimeout(() => { this.pending.delete(id); reject(new Error('CDP timeout: ' + method)); }, timeoutMs);\n      this.pending.set(id, { resolve, reject, timer });\n      this.ws.send(JSON.stringify(sessionId ? { id, method, params, sessionId } : { id, method, params }));\n    });\n  }\n\n  on(sessionId, method, fn) {\n    const k = (sessionId || '') + '|' + method;\n    if (!this.listeners.has(k)) this.listeners.set(k, new Set());\n    this.listeners.get(k).add(fn);\n    return () => this.listeners.get(k)?.delete(fn);\n  }\n\n  async newPage({ width = 1440, height = 900, dsf = 1, mobile = false, reducedMotion = false } = {}) {\n    const { targetId } = await this.send('Target.createTarget', { url: 'about:blank', newWindow: true });\n    const { sessionId } = await this.send('Target.attachToTarget', { targetId, flatten: true });\n    const p = new Page(this, targetId, sessionId);\n    await p.send('Page.enable');\n    await p.send('Runtime.enable');\n    await p.setViewport({ width, height, dsf, mobile });\n    if (reducedMotion) {\n      await p.send('Emulation.setEmulatedMedia', { features: [{ name: 'prefers-reduced-motion', value: 'reduce' }] });\n    }\n    return p;\n  }\n\n  async close() {\n    try { await this.send('Browser.close', {}, undefined, 3000); } catch {}\n    try { this.ws.close(); } catch {}\n    try { this.proc.kill(); } catch {}\n    await sleep(300);\n    try { rmSync(this.dir, { recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 3 }); } catch {}\n  }\n}\n\nexport class Page {\n  constructor(browser, targetId, sessionId) {\n    this.browser = browser; this.targetId = targetId; this.sessionId = sessionId;\n    this.consoleErrors = [];\n    browser.on(sessionId, 'Runtime.exceptionThrown', (p) => {\n      this.consoleErrors.push((p.exceptionDetails?.exception?.description || p.exceptionDetails?.text || '').slice(0, 300));\n    });\n    // Never let a JS dialog block the page.\n    browser.on(sessionId, 'Page.javascriptDialogOpening', () => {\n      this.send('Page.handleJavaScriptDialog', { accept: false }).catch(() => {});\n    });\n  }\n\n  send(method, params = {}, timeoutMs = 30000) {\n    return this.browser.send(method, params, this.sessionId, timeoutMs);\n  }\n\n  async setViewport({ width, height, dsf = 1, mobile = false }) {\n    this.viewport = { width, height, dsf, mobile };\n    await this.send('Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride', { width, height, deviceScaleFactor: dsf, mobile });\n    await this.send('Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled', { enabled: !!mobile });\n  }\n\n  // Navigates and resolves after the load event (or timeout), then waits `settleMs` for intros to finish.\n  async goto(url, { timeoutMs = 25000, settleMs = 1500 } = {}) {\n    let off;\n    const loaded = new Promise((resolve) => { off = this.browser.on(this.sessionId, 'Page.loadEventFired', () => resolve('load')); });\n    const nav = await this.send('Page.navigate', { url }, timeoutMs).catch((e) => ({ errorText: e.message }));\n    if (nav.errorText && !/ERR_ABORTED/.test(nav.errorText)) { off(); throw new Error('navigate: ' + nav.errorText); for (const { m, r: pr } of pictures) { if (m.contains(el) || el.contains(m)) continue; const ox = Math.min(r.right, pr.right) - Math.max(r.left, pr.left), oy = Math.min(r.bottom, pr.bottom) - Math.max(r.top, pr.top); if (ox > 0 && oy > 0) over += ox * oy; } }\n      }\n    }\n    if (total >= 4 && hidden / total >= 0.2) covered.push({ text: label(el, direct), share: Math.round((hidden / total) * 100) / 100 });\n    if (cutTop) clipped.push({ text: label(el, direct) });\n    if (pinned && area && over / area >= 0.15) pinnedOver.push({ text: label(el, direct), share: Math.min(1, Math.round((over / area) * 100) / 100) });\n  }\n  hitStyle.remove();\n  // 2. how much of the screen holds anything: text glyph boxes, media, or a ground that differs from the page's\n  const opaque = (c) => c && c !== 'transparent' && !/rgba\\([^)]*,\\s*0\\)$/.test(c);\n  const pageBg = [document.body, document.documentElement].map((e) => getComputedStyle(e).backgroundColor).find(opaque) || 'rgb(255, 255, 255)';\n  const textRects = [];\n  const walker = document.createTreeWalker(document.body, NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT); const rg = document.createRange();\n  for (let n = walker.nextNode(); n; n = walker.nextNode()) {\n    if (!n.nodeValue.trim() || !n.parentElement) continue; const pcs = getComputedStyle(n.parentElement); if (pcs.visibility === 'hidden' || +pcs.opacity < 0.2) continue;\n    rg.selectNodeContents(n); for (const r of rg.getClientRects()) if (r.bottom > 0 && r.top < H && r.width > 1) textRects.push(r);\n  }\n  let filled = 0, samples = 0;\n  for (let gx = 0; gx < 24; gx++) for (let gy = 0; gy < 15; gy++) {\n    const x = (gx + 0.5) * (W / 24), y = (gy + 0.5) * (H / 15); samples++;\n    if (textRects.some((r) => x >= r.left - 6 && x <= r.right + 6 && y >= r.top - 4 && y <= r.bottom + 4)) { filled++; continue; }\n    let el = document.elementFromPoint(x, y);\n    for (let i = 0; el && i < 6 && el !== document.body && el !== document.documentElement; i++, el = el.parentElement) {\n      if (/^(IMG|VIDEO|CANVAS|PICTURE|svg|IFRAME)$/.test(el.tagName) || el.closest('svg')) { filled++; break; }\n      const cs = getComputedStyle(el);\n      if (cs.backgroundImage !== 'none') { filled++; break; }\n      const bg = cs.backgroundColor; if (bg !== 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)' && bg !== 'transparent') { if (bg !== pageBg) filled++; break; }\n    }\n  }\n  // 3. the large text in view, to spot one statement held on screen for screen after screen\n  const big = [...new Set([...document.querySelectorAll('h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, p, blockquote')].filter((el) => { const r = el.getBoundingClientRect(); return parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).fontSize) >= 32 && r.top >= -4 && r.bottom <= H + 4 && r.height > 0; }).map((el) => (el.innerText || '').replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim().slice(0, 60)).filter((t) => t.length >= 4))];\n  return { covered, clipped, pinnedOver, filled: Math.round((filled / samples) * 100) / 100, big, y: Math.round(scrollY) };\n}\n\n// Dominant colours of a screenshot. Runs inside any page; takes a data: URL.\nexport async function palette(dataUrl) {\n  const img = new Image(); img.src = dataUrl; await img.decode();\n  const w = 96, h = Math.max(1, Math.round((96 * img.height) / img.width));\n  const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = w; c.height = h;\n  const x = c.getContext('2d', { willReadFrequently: true }); x.drawImage(img, 0, 0, w, h);\n  const d = x.getImageData(0, 0, w, h).data; const bins = new Map();\n  for (let i = 0; i < d.length; i += 4) {\n    const k = (d[i] >> 4) << 8 | (d[i + 1] >> 4) << 4 | (d[i + 2] >> 4);\n    const b = bins.get(k) || [0, 0, 0, 0]; b[0] += d[i]; b[1] += d[i + 1]; b[2] += d[i + 2]; b[3]++; bins.set(k, b);\n  }\n  const total = w * h;\n  return [...bins.values()].sort((a, b) => b[3] - a[3]).slice(0, 6).map((b) => ({\n    color: '#' + [0, 1, 2].map((i) => Math.round(b[i] / b[3]).toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join(''), share: Math.round((b[3] / total) * 100) / 100,\n  }));\n}\n",
  "bundled-skills/design-taste-frontend/scripts/lib/rules.mjs": "// Turns probe() metrics into findings. Each finding: { level: 'FAIL'|'WARN', id, message, fix }.\n// FAIL = a banned tell or a broken page; the work is not done while one remains.\n// WARN = usually wrong; keep only with a reason you could say out loud to a designer.\n\nconst inRange = (h, a, b) => (a <= b ? h >= a && h <= b : h >= a || h <= b);\n\n// Colour families this skill treats as generated-page signatures.\nexport function colourFamily(hsl) {\n  if (!hsl) return null;\n  const { h, s, l } = hsl;\n  if (inRange(h, 22, 62) && s >= 0.16 && l >= 0.88 && l < 0.995) return 'cream';\n  if (inRange(h, 6, 30) && s >= 0.38 && s <= 0.85 && l >= 0.42 && l <= 0.72) return 'terracotta';\n  if (inRange(h, 244, 295) && s >= 0.42 && l >= 0.3 && l <= 0.8) return 'ai-purple';\n  return null;\n}\n\nconst hexToHsl = (hex) => {\n  const n = parseInt(hex.slice(1), 16); const r = (n >> 16) / 255, g = ((n >> 8) & 255) / 255, b = (n & 255) / 255;\n  const mx = Math.max(r, g, b), mn = Math.min(r, g, b); const l = (mx + mn) / 2; let h = 0, s = 0;\n  if (mx !== mn) { const d = mx - mn; s = l > 0.5 ? d / (2 - mx - mn) : d / (mx + mn); h = mx === r ? (g - b) / d + (g < b ? 6 : 0) : mx === g ? (b - r) / d + 2 : (r - g) / d + 4; h *= 60; }\n  return { h: Math.round(h), s, l };\n};\n\nexport function judge(m, { width = m.viewport.w, allow = [] } = {}) {\n  const out = [];\n  const add = (level, id, message, fix) => { if (!allow.includes(id)) out.push({ level, id, width, message, fix }); };\n  const mobile = width < 600;\n\n  // --- headlines\n  // A title holds to two lines. A statement (a paragraph, quotation or list item set large) may run\n  // longer, but only at statement size; set at display size it is a headline again. In blind tests jurors\n  // read any large sentence of three lines or more as a long headline, so statement size is kept modest.\n  const stmtMaxPx = width < 600 ? 24 : width < 1100 ? 32 : 36;\n  const stmtMaxLines = width < 600 ? 4 : 3;\n  const isStatement = (h) => h.kind === 'statement' && h.size <= stmtMaxPx;\n  const long = m.headings.filter((h) => h.lines > 2 && !isStatement(h));\n  if (long.length) {\n    add('FAIL', 'headline-lines', `${long.length} headline(s) wrap past two lines at ${width}px: ` + long.slice(0, 4).map((h) => `\"${h.text.slice(0, 48)}\" → ${h.lines} lines (${h.words} words, ${h.size}px${h.kind === 'statement' ? ', a paragraph set above ' + stmtMaxPx + 'px' : ''})`).join('; '),\n      'Cut words first (a headline is a title, not a sentence). Then give it a wider measure. Lower the size only as a last resort and never below the scale you chose. A real statement paragraph belongs in a <p> or <blockquote> at ' + stmtMaxPx + 'px or less.');\n  }\n  const longStatements = m.headings.filter((h) => isStatement(h) && h.lines > stmtMaxLines);\n  if (longStatements.length) {\n    add('WARN', 'statement-length', `${longStatements.length} large-set statement(s) run past ${stmtMaxLines} lines at ${width}px: ` + longStatements.slice(0, 3).map((h) => `\"${h.text.slice(0, 40)}…\" → ${h.lines} lines at ${h.size}px`).join('; '),\n      'A statement set large is about 30 words. Cut it, or set the rest as ordinary body text.');\n  }\n  if (m.hero && m.hero.words > 10) add('WARN', 'hero-words', `Hero headline is ${m.hero.words} words (\"${m.hero.text.slice(0, 60)}\"). Gallery median is 5.`, 'Say the one thing. Move the rest to the supporting line.');\n  if (m.headingSummary.mixedFontHeadings) add('WARN', 'mixed-font-headline', `${m.headingSummary.mixedFontHeadings} headline(s) switch typeface or to italic mid-line (the \"one italic serif word\" move).`, 'Set the whole headline in one face. Emphasis comes from the words.');\n\n  // --- banned furniture\n  if (m.eyebrows.length) {\n    add('FAIL', 'eyebrow', `${m.eyebrows.length} eyebrow/kicker label(s) above headings: ` + m.eyebrows.slice(0, 5).map((e) => `\"${e.text}\"${e.pill ? ' (pill)' : ''} above \"${e.above}\"`).join('; '),\n      'Delete them. If the label carried real information, fold it into the headline or the supporting sentence.');\n  }\n  if (m.type.monoProseShare > 0) {\n    add('FAIL', 'mono', `Monospace type outside code: ${m.type.monoFamilies.join(', ')} — e.g. ${m.type.monoSamples.slice(0, 4).map((s) => `\"${s}\"`).join(', ')}`,\n      'Set it in the text face. Monospace is for literal code inside <pre>/<code> only.');\n  }\n  if (m.numbered.length) {\n    add('FAIL', 'numbering', `Decorative index numbers: ${m.numbered.slice(0, 6).map((n) => `\"${n.text}\"`).join(', ')}`,\n      'Remove them. If order truly matters, write it into the words (\"First, …\") or use a real <ol>.');\n  }\n  if (m.type.microLabels >= 3) add('FAIL', 'micro-label', `${m.type.microLabels} tiny uppercase letter-spaced labels (e.g. ${m.type.microSamples.slice(0, 4).map((s) => `\"${s}\"`).join(', ')}).`, 'Use sentence-case text at a readable size, or delete the label.');\n  else if (m.type.microLabels > 0) add('WARN', 'micro-label', `${m.type.microLabels} tiny uppercase letter-spaced label(s): ${m.type.microSamples.slice(0, 3).map((s) => `\"${s}\"`).join(', ')}`, 'Prefer sentence case at body size.');\n  if (m.page.emoji.length) add('FAIL', 'emoji', `Emoji in the page: ${m.page.emoji.join(' ')}`, 'Remove. Use words or real imagery.');\n\n  // --- surfaces\n  const s = m.surfaces;\n  if (s.gradients) add('FAIL', 'gradient', `${s.gradients} gradient fill(s): ${s.gradientSamples.slice(0, 3).join(' | ')}`, 'Use a flat colour or a real image. The only gradient allowed by default is a neutral scrim over a photo for legibility.');\n  if (s.gradientText) add('FAIL', 'gradient-text', `${s.gradientText} gradient-filled text element(s).`, 'Solid colour text.');\n  if (s.shadowStatic) add('FAIL', 'shadow', `${s.shadowStatic} box-shadow(s) on elements at rest: ${s.shadowSamples.slice(0, 3).join(' | ')}`, 'Remove. Separate surfaces with a tone step or space. Shadows are for things that really float (menus, dialogs, sticky bars).');\n  if (s.textShadow) add('FAIL', 'text-shadow', `${s.textShadow} text-shadow(s).`, 'Remove; fix legibility with a scrim or a different crop.');\n  if (m.buttons.withGradient || m.buttons.withShadow) add('FAIL', 'button-fx', `Buttons with ${m.buttons.withGradient ? 'gradient fill' : ''}${m.buttons.withGradient && m.buttons.withShadow ? ' and ' : ''}${m.buttons.withShadow ? 'shadow/glow' : ''}.`, 'Flat fill, one colour.');\n  if (s.hairlines) add(s.hairlines >= 2 ? 'FAIL' : 'WARN', 'hairline', `${s.hairlines} thin rule(s)/divider line(s): ${s.hairlineSamples.slice(0, 4).join(' | ')}`, 'Delete. Separate with space, a tone change, or scale. Lines are only for real tables and form fields.');\n  if (s.outlinedBoxes >= 3) add('FAIL', 'outlined-box', `${s.outlinedBoxes} boxes drawn with a 1px outline.`, 'Define a surface by its fill (one tone step from the page) or leave the content unboxed.');\n  else if (s.outlinedBoxes) add('WARN', 'outlined-box', `${s.outlinedBoxes} box(es) drawn with a 1px outline.`, 'Prefer a filled surface or no box.');\n  if (s.dashed) add('WARN', 'dashed', `${s.dashed} dashed/dotted border(s).`, 'Remove unless it is a real drop zone.');\n  if (s.blurred > 1) add('WARN', 'glass', `${s.blurred} backdrop-blur surfaces.`, 'One blurred sticky bar at most;
